Jordan — attaching the artifacts Ben pulled plus a quick note:

Attachments: privatelink_manifest.csv; keystore-segmentation-diagram.pdf; control-inventory-sheet.xlsx

Summary:
- PrivateLink endpoints: three interface endpoints (eu-west-1) terminating into account rdw-eu-prod-01 (10.0.45.0/24) and a standby account rdw-eu-standby-01. CSV column layout: endpoint_id, service, region, target_account, vpc_id, subnet_ids.
- Keys: All tenant data keys for EU tenants are customer-key-supportable: the primary CMKs for data-at-rest are customer-managed keys (CMKs) in the customer's KMS when customers request BYOK. For standard hosted EU tenants we use Redwood-managed CMKs partitioned in the eu-west-1 partition (arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/xxxxx).
- Cross-region KMS calls: Our diagnostics tooling (ops debug agent) only reads encrypted metadata and will never perform decrypt operations in another region for tenant data keys. Operational runbooks route diagnostic logs to rdw-ops-eu region; any key material used for debug traces is separate and stored in an ops-only CMK with least-privilege.

Notes / caveats:
- If Halcyon requests a fully customer-managed BYOK flow, that will require a short onboarding step (DocuSign key agreement) and KMS grants; timelines are typically 3–5 business days.
- Backup/replication: snapshot copies for cold backups remain in eu-west-1 and are encrypted by the same EU CMKs; we do not replicate customer encrypted snapshots to other regions for EU-only deployments.

I can produce a 1-page auditor summary (PDF) that pulls these points together and highlights where the keys live. Ben — please confirm the CSV rows match what you exported and that the manifest includes endpoint ARNs.

— Irene
